body:
`tests.yml` sets `concurrency: group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` with
cancel-in-progress, so a new push supersedes the running verification. Separately, `E2E Tests (SPA)`
waits for the PR head's own immutable `sha-<commit>` image, published by "Build & Push - Dev -
Split Strategy", which has its OWN concurrency group and is cancelled by the same new push.

The two interact badly. On a new push:
  - the OLD Test Suite's `Build & Push` is cancelled  -> `sha-<old>` is NEVER published;
  - the OLD Test Suite's E2E job is NOT reliably cancelled with it, and can even START afterwards;
  - it then waits for an image that can never exist, staying `in_progress` indefinitely;
  - because it still holds the concurrency group, the NEWEST run sits at `status=pending` with
    ZERO jobs dispatched, looking like ordinary queueing.

OBSERVED 2026-08-29 on PR #1956:
  Build & Push  5a12cfeb48 = cancelled  (so sha-5a12cfeb48 never published)
  Test Suite    5a12cfeb48 = in_progress, E2E started 15:02:52Z, still running at 15:48:29Z
                             (45 min; a healthy E2E run is ~6.6 min)
  Test Suite    eac39ddf1a = cancelled
  Test Suite    c4bd75967b = pending, 0 jobs, created 14:56:58Z, updatedAt never moved
`gh run cancel` was submitted and did NOT take. `POST /actions/runs/<id>/force-cancel` cleared it,
and the newest run moved to in_progress within seconds.

## Why it matters beyond the delay

The failure presents as "CI is busy". `status=pending` with no jobs is indistinguishable from
queueing behind other branches, so the natural response is to keep waiting — indefinitely. This is
the same family as F-493b49 (cancel-in-progress discarding main's runs): a cancellation policy that
is correct for the job it names, and wrong for a job that depends on that job's artifact.

## Fix shapes (not implemented; needs an operator/CI-owner call)

1. Make the E2E job's image wait BOUNDED — fail fast with a stated reason when the producer run for
   its own SHA is cancelled/failed, rather than waiting out the job timeout. The workflow already
   has precedent for this: manual E2E "fails immediately when that tag was not prepared, rather
   than waiting for a producer that was never started".
2. Or put E2E and its image producer in the SAME concurrency group so they are cancelled together.

A job killed by `timeout-minutes` reports as `cancelled`, not `failure` (already documented in the
summary job), so even the eventual timeout would not have surfaced this as a failure.

## Telling this apart from ordinary slowness — do this FIRST

The force-cancel recipe below is only reachable once you suspect a wedge at all, and the PR-level
view cannot help you: a wedged run and a genuinely slow one both render as "checks pending". The
discriminator is the JOB COUNT on the newest run.

    gh run view <id> --json status,jobs --jq '{status, jobcount:(.jobs|length)}'

  - **jobcount 0 while `status=pending`** -> WEDGED. Nothing was ever dispatched; it is holding the
    concurrency group. Force-cancel it (below).
  - **jobcount > 0 with some green and one in_progress** -> real work, genuinely slow. Leave it.

Contributed by the CWNG MY LIBRARY session, 2026-08-29, from a measured comparison: it had absorbed
four ci-timeouts as "the E2E lane is just slow" and re-checked rather than keep believing it. Its
runs came back jobcount 4 (Fast Tests, Detect changed paths, Frontend Build green; Integration
in_progress) — the opposite reading to this finding's, and correctly diagnosed by the same one-call
probe. Both failure modes are common enough that the probe is worth running before either
conclusion.
title: A superseded Test Suite run wedges forever waiting for an image its own producer was cancelled from publishing, and holds the concurrency group against the newest run
